Package system requirements

Source: R/system_requirements.R
pac_system_requirements.Rd

Report the SystemRequirements fields declared by a package and its dependencies. These fields are free text and can describe optional or platform-specific requirements; this function does not check whether they are installed or resolve dependency version constraints. It reports the installed versions or the versions selected from the repository indexes.

Usage

pac_system_requirements(
  pac,
  fields = c("Depends", "Imports", "LinkingTo"),
  lib.loc = .libPaths(),
  local = TRUE,
  recursive = TRUE,
  recursive_fields = c("Depends", "Imports", "LinkingTo"),
  repos = biocran_repos()
)

Arguments

pac

character a package name.

fields

Dependency fields to follow for the requested package. In addition to the values described in pac_deps(), character(0) considers only the requested package.

lib.loc

character vector of search paths with local packages. Default: .libPaths()

local

Use installed packages when TRUE (the default), or current source packages in repos when FALSE.

recursive

Follow dependencies recursively. Default: TRUE.

recursive_fields

Dependency fields to follow for indirect dependencies. Defaults to c("Depends", "Imports", "LinkingTo"). Accepts the same values as fields, including character(0).

repos

Repositories to use for source packages when local = FALSE. Default: biocran_repos(). Bulk repository metadata is used when available; otherwise source archives are downloaded to read their DESCRIPTION files.

Value

A named list, similar to tools::package_dependencies(). Names are package names, starting with pac, and each element is a character vector of declared system requirements. The SystemRequirements field is split on top-level commas and semicolons (not inside parentheses), with whitespace normalized; fields written as sentences are kept whole. Splitting is heuristic because the field is free text. Packages without a declared field have character(0). Dependencies missing from the library or repositories have NA_character_ and produce a warning, because their own dependencies cannot be assessed. The "versions" attribute is a named character vector with the installed or repository versions. Use unique(unlist(result)) to get all requirements.

Details

With recursive = FALSE, only the package and its direct dependencies are considered. With recursive = TRUE, dependencies are followed recursively. By default, Suggests and Enhances are only followed for the requested package when included in fields; indirect dependencies use recursive_fields. R and its base packages are excluded from the dependencies, but the requested package is always included.

Note

By default, source repository indexes are filtered for the current R version and platform. Bulk metadata and downloaded DESCRIPTION fields are cached for 30 minutes. A missing SystemRequirements field does not guarantee that a package has no system requirements. Bioconductor bulk metadata can normalize whitespace in the declared field.

Examples

pac_system_requirements("stats", fields = character())
#> $stats
#> character(0)
#> 
#> attr(,"versions")
#>   stats 
#> "4.6.2" 
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
pac_system_requirements("curl", recursive = FALSE)
pac_system_requirements("sf", local = FALSE, repos = "https://cran.r-project.org")
sf <- pac_system_requirements("sf", fields = "most", local = FALSE)
sf[["sf"]]
# all requirements of sf and its dependencies
unique(unlist(sf, use.names = FALSE))
} # }
